comparison: Both evaluate the technical quality and successful structural determination of APC/C complexes (C23, C24, C157, C158). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of resolution, functional, and mass spec data, while peer reviewers highlight the high technical quality as a major strength.

Perfect agreement on conservation of APC/C architecture between species (C2, C25, C149, C150, C160, C161). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites structural comparison in Figures 1-4, while peer reviewers affirm 'remarkable similarity' and 'widespread similarities in fundamental structural features.'

Perfect agreement on the major finding that E2-binding conformation differs between species (C5, C33, C125, C126, C127). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the mechanism is not fully defined, and peer reviewers explicitly discuss this as showing 'enhancement of E2 binding in yeast depends on other, as yet undiscovered, mechanisms.'

Perfect agreement on the absence of autoinhibitory loop and non-conservation of CDC20 activation mechanism (C6, C142, C143, C155). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of structural and functional data, while peer reviewers confirm this as an 'important difference' with 'unknown mechanisms' for yeast activation.

Both address phosphorylation-mediated CDH1 inhibition conservation (C3, C108-C115, C154). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes structural mapping of phosphorylation sites to interfaces, while peer reviewers affirm 'mechanism of CDH1 inhibition by phosphorylation appears conserved across kingdoms.'

Perfect agreement on the unusual APC4 architecture in S. cerevisiae (C41, C42, C43, C44, C45). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergence with AlphaFold2 predictions and appropriate speculation about species-specificity, while peer reviewers accept this as part of valuable structural characterization.

Both address the absence of APC2ZBM in S. cerevisiae (C38, C39). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites sequence analysis and absence in cryo-EM data, while peer reviewers accept this as part of documented structural differences between species.

Strong agreement on detailed structural characterization of smaller subunits and their interactions (C50-C58, C63-C65, C70-C74, C79-C83, C94). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes AlphaFold2 guidance at moderate resolution, while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive structural analysis without specific concerns.

Both address CDH1NTD structure and interactions (C104-C107), though peer review groups this with phosphorylation conservation claims. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes direct visualization of structural features, while peer reviewers affirm the conservation findings.

Perfect agreement on different conformational mechanisms between human and yeast for coactivator-mediated activation (C128-C133). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes functional consequences remain incompletely defined, while peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive comparison providing 'valuable insights.'

Both evaluate claims about phosphorylation effects and activation mechanism (C144, C145, C156). Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval cites partial phosphorylation in control and speculative mechanism, while peer reviewers express concern about phosphorylation validation robustness but accept structural interpretations with caveats.

Both address phosphorylation validation issues (C146, C147, C148). Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the 'unphosphorylated' control was partially phosphorylated, complicating interpretation. Peer reviewers raise significant concerns about lack of quantitative mass spec data and extent of site modification.

Perfect agreement on absence of APC15 in S. cerevisiae (C116, C117). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites sequence alignment and absence in cryo-EM data, while peer reviewers accept this species-specific difference as part of comprehensive structural comparison.

OpenEval evaluates conservation of APC7 structure and species-specific meiotic functions (C85-C93) as SUPPORTED based on structural conservation and cited functional data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates disease mechanism claims (C151-C153) as SUPPORTED based on cited prior research (Ferguson et al., 2022). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about AMER1 and colorectal cancer.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background/context claims (C1, C7-C22, C26-C31, C46-C49, C98-C101, C120-C124, C134-C141, C159, C162-C167) as SUPPORTED, noting these represent established knowledge from prior research. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates comparative context claims about human APC/C features (C4, C59-C62, C68, C75-C78, C96, C102-C103, C119) as SUPPORTED, noting these are from cited research or appropriately qualified speculations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific comparative claims.

OpenEval evaluates structural inferences about IDP stabilization and functional hypotheses (C32, C66, C36, C44) as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable inferences but lack of direct functional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific inferential claims.
